title: Drag down to copy values in st.data_editor doesn't work for the rightmost column if there is a scrollbar
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [x] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [x] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

It's not possible to drag down (using the "+") to copy values in the `st.data_editor` for the rightmost column if there is a scrollbar. It's either not possible to find the "+" or if it's found, then the values are not copied.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import pandas as pd
import streamlit as st

df_rank = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "Fleet customer": [
            "Volvo Fleet Demo AB",
            "Nordic Lease Partner",
            "City Mobility Co",
            "Green Transport AS",
            "LogiNorth AB",
            "Urban Move Oy",
            "Swift Logistics AB",
            "EcoDrive Solutions",
            "Metro Fleet Services",
            "Nordic Fleet Management",
        ],
        "Order count": [420, 315, 288, 241, 198, 175, 160, 145, 130, 120],
        "Margin": [
            58.2,
            44.7,
            39.1,
            31.6,
            26.8,
            23.5,
            21.0,
            18.7,
            16.5,
            15.0,
        ],
    }
)
st.data_editor(df_rank, height=200)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Hover over a cell in the "Margin" column until you see the "+" sign
2. Click and try to drag down to copy

### Expected Behavior

I expect to be able to easily find the "+" sign and drag down to copy the values of the cell, as it works for the "Order count" column in the example.

### Current Behavior

Nothing will be copied and you have only moved the scrollbar. Often it's not even possible to find the "+".

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.56.0
- Python version: 3.12
- Operating System: Debian 12
- Browser: Chrome, firefox, edge


### Additional Information

_No response_

**If this issue affects you, please react with a 👍 (thumbs up emoji) to the initial post.**

Your feedback helps us prioritize which bugs to investigate and address first.

![Views](https://api.views-badge.org/badge/st-issue-15295)

This is a bug report for `st.data_editor`: the drag-to-fill ("+") handle on cells in the rightmost column is obscured by the dataframe's vertical scrollbar (rendered by the underlying `glide-data-grid` library). Because the scrollbar sits on top of the cell's bottom-right corner, mouse interactions hit the scrollbar instead of the fill handle, so click-and-drag scrolls the grid instead of copying values down. The reporter's example uses `height=200` to force a scrollbar, but the same problem occurs whenever the grid overflows (e.g. `use_container_width=True` with enough rows).

This appears to be a duplicate of the already-confirmed issue #9971 (status:confirmed, priority:P3, upstream). A known CSS workaround is to apply `scrollbar-gutter: stable both-edges` to the `.dvn-scroller` element so the scrollbar no longer overlaps the fill handle, but this introduces whitespace on the right edge of the header. A proper fix likely needs to land upstream in `glide-data-grid` (see `frontend/lib/src/components/widgets/DataFrame/styled-components.ts` where `.dvn-scroller` overflow is configured, and `useDataFrameCapabilities.ts` which enables `supportsFillHandle`).

### Related Issues

- [#9971 — Unable to drag to copy a value from one cell to a range of cells in the rightmost column of st.data_editor](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9971): Same root cause (scrollbar overlapping the fill handle in the rightmost column); already confirmed, prioritized P3, and tagged `upstream`. This new issue should likely be closed as a duplicate.
- [#11998 — Minor styling issue with data editor causing highlight color to be clipped](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/11998): Another confirmed `upstream` data-editor styling/clipping issue in the same scrollbar/edge area of the grid.
- [#8504 — Prevent layout shift caused by scrollbars](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/8504): Related general request to use `scrollbar-gutter` to reserve space for scrollbars — the same CSS mechanism that works around this bug.
